title: DB migrations: add guardrails (idempotency checks, lock timeouts, safer defaults) for Private upgrades
author: Michael Nguyen
release_notes:
- Adds migration safety guardrails used during Private upgrades: advisory locks, lock/statement timeouts, idempotency validation, and "safe default" patterns for schema changes.
- Improves migration logging and surfaces actionable errors to upgrade tooling.
- No user-facing API changes; behavior change is limited to migration execution and failure mode (fail-fast with clearer remediation).
body:
Title: DB migrations: add guardrails (idempotency checks, lock timeouts, safer defaults) for Private upgrades

Context
We’ve had multiple upgrade-related incidents/near-misses where a migration either (a) blocked application traffic for longer than expected due to long lock waits, (b) partially applied and then re-ran in an unsafe way, or (c) took a non-backward-compatible path that required perfect ordering across control-plane/data-plane rollouts. The most recent customer-visible case is SUP-18421 (upgrade failed during DB migration; required manual intervention and extended downtime).

This PR adds a set of guardrails to make migrations safer by default in Private environments:
- predictable lock acquisition behavior (timeouts + fail-fast)
- explicit idempotency checks (detect partial/duplicate application earlier)
- safer schema patterns (additive/expand-then-contract defaults, avoid non-null without backfill, avoid table rewrites)
- better structured logging so installer can present actionable remediation and so SRE can correlate upgrade windows

Goals
- Reduce upgrade-induced outages by preventing migrations from waiting indefinitely on locks.
- Make reruns safe and detectable (idempotency validation + consistent bookkeeping).
- Encourage backward-compatible schema evolution so CP/DP phase separation remains valid.
- Keep changes compatible with existing migration tooling and deployment modes.

Non-goals
- Rewriting existing historical migrations.
- Introducing multi-hop migration automation across many majors.

What changed
1) Migration execution guardrails (Postgres)
- Enforce lock timeout and statement timeout for all migration sessions.
  - Default lock_timeout: 5s
  - Default statement_timeout: 15m
  - Both are configurable via env/config for Private deployments.
- Acquire an advisory lock keyed by (service, schema) before applying any migrations to prevent concurrent migration runners during rollouts.
- Ensure all migration steps run in a controlled transaction mode (transactional where possible; explicit non-transactional allow-list).

2) Idempotency & partial-apply detection
- Validate migration history before applying:
  - Detect duplicate version entries.
  - Detect checksum mismatch for already-applied migrations (when a migration file changed between builds).
  - Detect “dirty” state from interrupted runs and fail with explicit remediation steps.
- Add a small helper that marks a migration as "started" and "completed" with timestamps for better debugging, while remaining compatible with the existing schema_migrations table (no breaking schema change).

3) Backward-compatible schema defaults
- New helpers/patterns used by upcoming Private upgrade work:
  - Add columns as nullable + backfill + set default + then (optionally) enforce NOT NULL in a later release.
  - Avoid blocking index creation (use CONCURRENTLY where supported and safe).
  - Prefer additive enums/polymorphic refs rather than destructive renames.
- Update a handful of existing in-tree migrations that were in-flight (unreleased) to follow the safer patterns (no changes to already-shipped migration versions).

4) Observability & operator UX
- Structured logs emitted per migration:
  - migration_version, migration_name, phase (acquire_lock/apply/verify), duration_ms
  - lock_timeout_ms, statement_timeout_ms
  - blocked_by_pid (when available) for lock timeouts
- Errors are categorized with remediation text intended for installer surface area:
  - LOCK_TIMEOUT: "retry after clearing blocking transaction; see query to identify blocker"
  - DIRTY_STATE: "manual verification required; see steps"
  - CHECKSUM_MISMATCH: "artifact mismatch; verify bundle/version pin"

Implementation details
- Config keys
  - REDWOOD_DB_MIGRATIONS_LOCK_TIMEOUT (default: 5s)
  - REDWOOD_DB_MIGRATIONS_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT (default: 15m)
  - REDWOOD_DB_MIGRATIONS_ADVISORY_LOCK (default: enabled)
- Advisory lock key is derived from a stable hash of (db_name + schema_name + service_name) to avoid collisions across services sharing a cluster.
- Lock timeout handling
  - We set local session settings at the start of each migration transaction.
  - On lock timeout, we emit the blocker info when obtainable and abort without retrying in-process (retry is handled by upgrade orchestration to keep behavior deterministic).

Files / areas touched (high level)
- services/control-plane/db/migrate/*
- services/common/db/migrations_runner/*
- services/common/db/postgres/lock_helpers.*
- docs/internal/private-upgrades/migration-guardrails.md
- tests/db/migrations_guardrails_test.*

Commits (summary)
- db: add advisory lock + timeout config for migration runner
- db: add migration history validation + dirty state detection
- db: structured logs + categorized errors for upgrade surfaces
- migrations: refactor unreleased migrations to use safe additive patterns
- tests: add integration tests for lock timeout and checksum mismatch cases
- docs: add "Migration guardrails" guidance for Private upgrade runbook

Testing
- Unit tests for history validation, checksum mismatch detection, and advisory lock behavior.
- Integration test (Postgres) that simulates:
  - long-running transaction holding an exclusive lock -> migration fails with LOCK_TIMEOUT and prints blocker pid query
  - dirty state -> fails with DIRTY_STATE and remediation text
  - checksum mismatch -> fails with CHECKSUM_MISMATCH (useful for air-gapped bundle mismatch debugging)
- Manual: applied on staging Private environment with synthetic traffic during upgrade window; verified CP/DP phased rollout does not deadlock.

Rollout / risk
- Low-to-medium risk: touches migration execution path. Mitigated by:
  - conservative timeouts + config overrides
  - fail-fast behavior (previous behavior was indefinite waiting)
  - additional logging for quick diagnosis
- Intended to be a prerequisite for the Private upgrade + rollback mechanism work (installer will treat these error categories as deterministic failure modes).

Reviewer notes / requests
- SRE asked that failure modes be explicit and that we don’t auto-retry inside the runner.
- Security asked that we avoid logging query contents or sensitive data; this PR only logs metadata and pids.

Review conversation (highlights)
- Sean Gallagher (SRE): "Can we ensure we never wait forever on locks? Also want the blocker PID surfaced so oncall can act quickly." Author: "Yes; lock_timeout is enforced via SET LOCAL; on timeout we attempt to query pg_locks/pg_stat_activity and include a suggested query with the blocker pid when available. No auto-retry in runner." Requested changes: add docs snippet to SRE runbook and ensure log fields are stable. Addressed in commit 4/6.
- Ethan Park: "Advisory lock keying: make sure multi-tenant DBs don’t collide and that services with separate schemas don’t block each other." Author: "Key includes db + schema + service; also added a unit test for key derivation stability." Approved after changes.
- Irene Choi: "Timeout defaults feel aggressive for large customers. Can we make them configurable and document recommended overrides?" Author: "Added env/config + docs table with guidance. Default statement timeout 15m; lock timeout 5s." Approved.
- Naomi Feldman: "Double-check logs don’t include SQL text or customer identifiers." Author: "Confirmed; only versions/names/timeouts/pids." Approved.
- Rafael Mendes: "How does this interact with installer rollback?" Author: "Fail-fast allows installer to stop before DP rollouts proceed; categorized errors map to planned remediation. This PR doesn’t implement rollback but is a dependency for deterministic upgrade state." Approved.

CI
- build-and-unit-tests: pass
- db-integration-tests: pass (added ~3m)
- lint: pass
- security-scan: pass

Merge
Merged via squash on 2025-06-07 by Connor O’Brien after approvals from Platform + SRE + Security. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-4844 to align installer surfaces with the new categorized errors and to ensure support bundles collect migration logs during upgrade windows.
